purpose: Non-card setting concept art and taste testing

sources.interpretation: Berserker concept and energy received positive feedback; fine rendering felt freaky. Test simplified painterly design in three non-card narrative concepts.

review_status: All three images strongly approved as visual direction; invented scenes remain exploratory.

images.title: The Still Flame
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Original high-fantasy CONCEPT ART for Breachline, independent of card briefs. Landscape PNG 1536 x 1024. Traditional oil/gouache/acrylic feeling, a beautiful finished colour study with confident economical brushwork. The user's newest taste feedback asks for LESS DETAIL: broad colour and light shapes, selective edges, human faces indicated with a few natural strokes, no pores or exaggerated eyes, no veins or individually rendered teeth, no microscopic texture covering the image. Rich colour variation, simple expressive silhouettes, suggested materials and meaningful action. Detail only where the visual story needs it. Sophisticated painted realism, not hyperrealism, not horror caricature, not flat cartoon, not polished 3D. Each piece has one clear visual idea. Use implied setting or a few monumental shapes; no cluttered city panoramas. No text, lettering, frames, UI, signature or watermark. Create original designs, no existing franchise characters or iconic objects.
SETTING: Present-day high fantasy, roughly 150 years after the Old Empire fell and the high gods became silent. New kingdoms are generally stable; this is a lived world, not universal apocalypse. Alignments are philosophies, not single nation states. The historical Bronze Age analogy is NOT the present-day costume style. Details of the Cataclysm's cause remain undecided.
SCENE: THE STILL FLAME. A wide, quiet, hopeful interior concept showing why people still believe after their gods fall silent. The composition is built around one immense EMPTY architectural niche and a broken roof opening, suggesting the scale of a vanished imperial sanctuary without showing a whole cathedral. Pale worn stone is painted in broad ivory and cool blue-grey planes. A shaft of clean morning light falls across a small daily act of compassion in the lower third.

A white-haired healer in simple ivory clothing kneels to wrap the hand of a seated road-weary traveller, their heads inclined toward the same task. A very small, soft warm light at the healer's fingertips hints at healing magic, not proof of the gods. Faces are small and loosely indicated; the tender, purposeful posture carries the feeling. A lion-headed escort with a soft golden mane and worn pale armour waits quietly at the side, barely more detailed than a few painted shapes. No red cape. These people are small against the architecture, but their pool of warmth is the living heart of the painting. One small burning brazier or lamp beside them echoes the name Still Flame.

Colour idea: luminous chalk ivory, pale sky blue, old ochre stone, a small concentrated honey-gold warmth among people. Subtle age and chipped surfaces, not every brick or crack. A few large vertical shapes, quiet negative space, lively painterly light. No god or statue of a known god, no apparition, no angels or halos, no battle, no grand magic. Faith persists through a modest act. This is a proposed concept scene, not an established campaign event. Illustration only; do not put the concept title in the image.
images.canon_status: Exploratory scene: Vigil faith and healing are established; this particular hall and characters are proposed.
images.story_relevance: Hope and ordinary care beneath the remains of the silent empire.
confirmed_preferences: Lighting should organize the scene and link its subjects. The Still Flame's dynamic warm light, visible brush strokes, integrated characters and small opening of blue sky are specifically loved.

Keep the economical, visible painted treatment of these approved concepts. Use meaningful selected detail, natural faces and varied brush scale; do not return to uncanny facial or surface microdetail.

SCENE: LIGHT WITHOUT AN ANSWER. A more intimate, inventive concept for Gnosis and the Brass Choir: magic treated as a practical craft and a future built by ordinary people. A clear dry blue evening beside a quiet canal. Only one old stone wall, one arch-shaped reflection and the water imply the surrounding city. No rain, crowded skyline or giant factory.

The focal action is an engineer in a work-worn deep-blue coat, a white woman around forty with her hair wrapped in a plain cloth, leaning over an open brass lamp housing at a small canal-side work platform. Her body turns away from the viewer in three-quarter view; her attention and hands align a suspended glass lens within a simple open brass ring. A small original four-legged brass assistant, about dog-sized with a curved teal-enamel shell, braces the ring with two fine jointed front limbs while its rear legs steady it on the platform. Its unusual creature-like mechanism should feel designed for its task, not a tiny human robot. Keep its silhouette clean and readable, not a nest of machinery.

A narrow cyan-white line of light through the lens reaches one previously dark lamp mounted on the opposite wall, which has just begun glowing softly amber. Its first reflection ripples across the canal. The engineer is absorbed, perhaps a small pleased smile only implied, not posing. This specific device is a proposed visual idea, not established world lore.

Colour idea: rich indigo water and twilight, teal and weathered brass, a restrained luminous cyan accent and one amber reflection. Clear shapes with painted edges, simplified face and machinery, warm-cool variation. Off-centre staging, medium-wide view, no hero portrait, no lightning spectacle. Capture discovery and practical intelligence. No text on diagrams or tools; no words in the painting.
images.canon_status: Exploratory scene: Gnosis treats magic as science; this experimental civic-lighting device is a proposal, not established lore.
images.story_relevance: Gnosis builds a useful future without waiting for the gods to return.
confirmed_preferences: Absorbed, purposeful activity is highly effective. In Light Without an Answer, the inventor's involvement in the lighting experiment and her small construct companion make the scene compelling.

Inventive creatures and constructs should feel like participants in the world. The little helper's design and role are strongly liked; preserve that functional imagination without repeating its exact anatomy or every scene's workshop.

Alignment identity can be clear without being heavy-handed. Light Without an Answer reads as Gnosis/blue through its activity, materials, light and palette without relying on all-blue colouring or repeated emblems.

images.prompt:

Create original designs, no existing franchise characters or iconic objects.
SETTING: Present-day high fantasy, roughly 150 years after the Old Empire fell and the high gods became silent. New kingdoms are generally stable; this is a lived world, not universal apocalypse. Alignments are philosophies, not single nation states. The historical Bronze Age analogy is NOT the present-day costume style. Details of the Cataclysm's cause remain undecided.
SCENE: ACROSS THE SILENCE. A creator-facing visual metaphor for this world's hidden cosmology, not a literal event the world's inhabitants understand. The high gods are alive but impossibly far away across primordial chaos. A summoner's connection somehow remains.

Paint a vast, imaginative, BEAUTIFUL space unlike a star-field or generic space nebula. Large slow folds of deep ultramarine, smoky violet and soft sea-green turn through a dim primordial expanse, like distant tidal masses or folds of unfinished land and cloud. Three or four coherent enormous shapes and large passages of dark quiet give depth; avoid all-over fractal noise, glitter, infinite filigree or hundreds of creatures. A far, pale-gold horizon, barely more than a sliver between two vast dark shapes, suggests unreachable warmth. Do not depict the gods themselves or any explanation of what caused the Cataclysm.

At the extreme lower-left foreground a very small human figure, seen from behind in a plain dark travelling coat, stands on a fragment of shadowed ground. No heroic stance: one shoulder slightly forward with tentative curiosity, body small and vulnerable. One sleeve is deliberately rolled back and a tiny warm golden scar is visible on the wrist. It is NOT being hidden. A single hair-thin gold thread travels from that wrist across an immense area of negative space and disappears toward the distant warm horizon. It reads as a fragile connection, not a beam or weapon. No raised casting arm, giant aura, portal ring or celestial throne.

Colour and scale carry the story. Deep blues, violet, small restrained sea-green passages and one impossibly distant note of warm light; keep shadows coloured. Render with broad translucent painterly glazes and selected opaque strokes, purposeful lost edges, minimal texture. The tiny figure is only a few convincing marks. Wonder, distance, uncertainty and fragile hope. No overt horror, eyes in the clouds, tentacles, visible monsters, starscape cliché or explanatory text. No concept title printed in the image.
images.canon_status: Creator-facing visual metaphor for the established secret cosmology. It does not establish a new journey, reveal, location or cause of the Cataclysm.
images.story_relevance: A summoner's surviving thread across the vast distance between the world and the gods.
confirmed_preferences: Story and image reinforce one another. Across the Silence is a strong positive reference because its figure, gold thread, distance and light make the gods and summoner connection visible.
Grand landscapes can include a small character to establish scale, point of view and emotional stakes. A figure need not fill the frame.
Some abstraction is welcome, especially for mystery, metaphysical ideas or enormous scale. Use it occasionally rather than making it the default for every image.
